name: Text as a whole
title: REPORT on the proposal for a directive of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Directives 2006/43/EC, 2013/34/EU, (EU) 2022/2464 and (EU) 2024/1760 as regards certain corporate sustainability reporting and due diligence requirements
part_text:
The European Parliament's legal affairs committee wants to loosen the European Union's rules on corporate sustainability reporting and due diligence. Fewer companies would have to report on their environmental and social impact: only those with more than 1,000 employees and a turnover above 450 million euro. Companies would also check fewer suppliers for human rights and environmental harm, and penalties would be capped at 5 percent of worldwide turnover. The committee's text is Parliament's starting position for talks with member states.

- Companies with over 1,000 employees and 450 million euro turnover must report; smaller suppliers face fewer information requests.
- Due diligence focuses on direct business partners, with penalties capped at 5 percent of turnover.
- Parliament votes in plenary, then negotiates the final text with EU governments.
